Existing backup setup intentionally grants future-table SELECT only to configured backup principal. This could explain another SELECT row; current snapshot does not identify it and setup must not be executed to resolve this review.

Existing incident/source explicitly shows new tables inherit default privileges even when migration has no GRANT. Owner-only countermeasures in that separate migration are not authority to revoke HRM access.

Existing route validates canonical app/migrator role separation, same live database and application privileged SET role exclusions. It does not join actual default-ACL write recipients to the canonical app identity; registry/runbook approve no finite recipient list.

primaryReferences.claim: Default privileges affect future creator-role objects; global and schema defaults can contribute to new table ACL.
FORCE RLS does not constrain TRUNCATE/REFERENCES; superuser/BYPASSRLS principals bypass row policies.
Ordinary index construction allows reads but blocks table writes; catalog size alone does not establish elapsed lock duration.
